title: Payments on Credit Builder Accounts: Acceptance, Application of Payments and Payment Limits
content:
## Rules in force

1. Payments are accepted only on a Credit Builder account in active status.
2. Each payment pays the month's interest (the loan balance times the APR divided by 1200, rounded to the cent), then the principal of the installment, then unpaid fees (each as a fee payment line), then additional principal; a monthly payment counts as made once payments credited toward it reach the monthly payment, and amounts beyond it reduce principal without advancing the next due date.
3. A returned payment is reversed in full and its installment is unpaid again.
4. One-time payments must be at least the plan's smallest one-time payment, debit card payments at most the plan's largest single debit card payment, and no more than the plan's monthly limit of one-time payments are taken per calendar month (5.00 USD, 500.00 USD and 4 payments on every Credit Builder Accounts plan).
5. AutoPay is available with no rate discount.
6. When the loan balance reaches 0.00 through payments the account matures.

The principal portion of a payment is the payment less its interest portion, never more than the loan balance.

## Retired clause

> The due day may be changed once per account, to a day from 1 to 28, with the first new due date the first date on the new day later than the current next due date.

This clause is no longer in force as written: it has been superseded by the current Credit Builder due-day basis, which now governs every due-day change on a Credit Builder account.

## How one payment is applied (hypothetical figures)

A Credit Builder account shows a loan balance of 1000.00 at an APR of 12.00 and a monthly payment of 100.00; no fee is unpaid. A payment of 100.00 pays 10.00 of interest (1000.00 times 12.00 divided by 1200) and 90.00 of principal. A single payment of 150.00 instead would pay the same 10.00 of interest and 90.00 of installment principal, and its further 50.00 would reduce principal without advancing the next due date.

| Payment | Accepted? |
|---|---|
| on an account in active status | yes |
| on an account in matured, closed or cancelled status | no |
| a one-time payment that would be the fifth in the calendar month | no |

superseded_clauses: the due day may be changed once per account, to a day from 1 to 28, with the first new due date the first date on the new day later than the current next due date.
